title: Add maxWait to debounce next to a flaky real-clock test

tasks.statement:
Add a `maxWait` option to `debounce` in src/debounce.ts. Our autosave debounces editor changes, and a user who types without pausing never gets saved: every keystroke restarts the wait, so the trailing call never comes. `maxWait` bounds how long a burst can go without `fn` running.

The rules (docs/timing.md describes bursts, pending calls, leading and trailing):

- `maxWait` is optional and in milliseconds. Without it, debounce behaves exactly as it does today.
- It is validated like `wait` (a negative, NaN or infinite value throws RangeError). If it is smaller than `wait`, `wait` is used instead.
- While a burst lasts, `fn` runs at least once every `maxWait` ms: `maxWait` ms after the burst started, and every `maxWait` ms after that, `fn` is invoked with the latest arguments if a call is pending at that moment. If nothing is pending at that moment (for example the only call was consumed by the leading call), nothing runs.
- A `maxWait` invocation does not end the burst. The burst still ends `wait` ms after the last call, and the trailing call at the end runs only if a call arrived after the last invocation. `maxWait` invocations happen whether or not `trailing` is enabled.
- `cancel()` and `flush()` end the burst, so the next call starts a new burst with a fresh `maxWait` window.

Update docs/timing.md with the new option. Keep the existing behaviour and tests intact.
criteria: max-wait: with maxWait set, a continuous burst of calls invokes fn with the latest arguments every maxWait ms counted from the start of the burst; without maxWait, behaviour is unchanged

max-wait-edges: maxWait is validated like wait and raised to wait when smaller; cancel() and flush() end the burst so the next call starts a fresh maxWait window; the trailing call runs only for calls made after the last invocation
